name: Mercury
description: Mercury is the smallest planet in the Solar System and the closest to the Sun. Despite its proximity to the Sun, it is not the hottest planet — Venus holds that distinction due to its thick greenhouse atmosphere. Mercury has virtually no atmosphere, resulting in extreme temperature swings.
atmosphere: Extremely thin exosphere: sodium, oxygen, hydrogen, helium, potassium
surface: Heavily cratered, similar to Earth's Moon; cliffs (scarps) up to 3 km high
core: Large iron core — 85% of the planet's radius
summary: Mercury is a battered, airless world with dramatic temperature extremes. Its oversized iron core and global magnetic field hint at a violent early history. MESSENGER revealed water ice in permanently shadowed polar craters. BepiColombo is en route to study Mercury in unprecedented detail.
interesting_facts: Mercury has the most extreme temperature variation of any planet: from -180°C to 430°C
A year on Mercury is just 88 Earth days, but a solar day lasts 176 Earth days
Mercury's iron core makes up 85% of its radius — proportionally the largest core of any planet
Despite being closest to the Sun, Mercury is not the hottest planet — Venus is
Mercury has water ice in permanently shadowed polar craters
The Caloris Basin is one of the largest impact craters in the Solar System at 1,550 km
Mercury is shrinking — its core is cooling and contracting, creating enormous cliffs called scarps
Mercury has no moons and no rings
Mercury was known to ancient civilizations — it was called Hermes by the Greeks
BepiColombo will arrive at Mercury in 2025 for a detailed orbital study

faq.a: Mercury is the smallest planet in the Solar System and the closest to the Sun, located 57.9 million km away. It has no atmosphere, no moons, and extreme temperatures.

faq.q: Why is Mercury not the hottest planet?
faq.a: Although Mercury is closest to the Sun, it has virtually no atmosphere to trap heat. Venus, with its thick CO₂ atmosphere creating a greenhouse effect, reaches 462°C — hotter than Mercury's maximum of 430°C.

faq.q: How long is a day on Mercury?
faq.a: A solar day on Mercury (sunrise to sunrise) is 176 Earth days — twice as long as its year of 88 Earth days! This is because Mercury rotates very slowly.
Yes! MESSENGER discovered water ice in permanently shadowed craters near Mercury's poles, where sunlight never reaches. The ice may have been delivered by comets and asteroids.
No, Mercury has no moons. Along with Venus, it is one of only two planets in the Solar System without a natural satellite.
Mercury has a large iron core (85% of its radius), a thin silicate mantle, and a heavily cratered rocky surface. Its high density suggests a metal-rich composition.
Yes. Mariner 10 flew by Mercury three times in 1974–75. MESSENGER orbited Mercury 2011–2015, mapping the entire surface. BepiColombo (ESA/JAXA) is currently en route, arriving in 2025.
Mercury has a diameter of 4,879 km — smaller than Jupiter's moon Ganymede. It is about 0.38 times Earth's size.

faq.q: What is the gravity on Mercury?
faq.a: Mercury's gravity is 3.7 m/s² — about 38% of Earth's gravity. A 70 kg person would weigh only 26.7 kg on Mercury.

faq.q: How far is Mercury from Earth?
faq.a: Mercury's distance from Earth varies between 77.3 million km (closest approach) and 222 million km (farthest), as both planets orbit the Sun at different speeds.
